市场担心的点：模型有优势吗？开源追上来之后还有必要开发你不算领先的模型吗？你们的模型是注重低端还是高端市场？我理解市场一直在惩罚META前期的乱花钱，小扎也做出了一些妥协：比如把算力放到自身业务上，比如直接卖算力等等，减轻前期投资ROI的一些疑虑
往未来去看，我认为META如果能做出来，有很好的一席之地，个人AI智能体，也是小扎这次财报强调的，有点和B2B业务类似，他们有C端的派发，我认为未来个人AGENT落地极有可能在META, AAPL, GOOG身上，这个市场可太大了。我认为META有未来，1年内会受利润率下降影响

text:
你再遇到谁唱空算力，你就把这篇博客甩他脸上🫡

Dwarkesh Patel在他新的Blog里面提出了一个很反直觉的判断：未来几年，AI算力价格可能上涨10倍以上。

过去大家默认，芯片性能不断提升，模型推理成本就会持续下降。

但算力的价格，最终并不只取决于生产成本，还取决于它能创造多少价值。

假设一张H100可以运行一个人类水平的软件工程师Agent。

按照目前软件工程师的市场价格，这张卡每年能够创造超过25万美元的价值，相当于今天H100现货租赁价格的15倍。

模型越聪明，同样一张GPU能够完成的工作越多，企业愿意为它支付的价格也就越高。

背后的矛盾很简单：

前沿AI公司的收入可以一年增长10倍，但全球AI算力供给大约只能增长3倍。

Anthropic和OpenAI的算力增长已经快于整个行业，GPU小时价格也在今年出现明显上涨。

Epoch AI估计，全球AI资本开支在2026年可能已经接近每年1万亿美元。

但主要问题是算力供给也很难无限加速。

先进制程受晶圆厂、EUV光刻机、封装、内存和电力共同限制。

仅一座1GW规模的AI数据中心，对应的芯片制造就需要大约350台EUV设备一整年的产能当量，整个供应链不可能因为模型突然变强，就立刻扩张十倍。

如果这个判断成立，会出现三个结果。

第一，前沿实验室的护城河会越来越深。

当GPU价格上涨十倍，没有收入的创业公司和研究团队，很难再和OpenAI、Anthropic竞争同一批算力。
领先公司可以用模型赚到的钱购买更多GPU，再训练更强的模型，形成一个越来越难追赶的循环。

第二，最强模型反而可以卖得更贵。

当每小时算力本身已经非常昂贵，使用一个能力较弱、需要消耗更多Token才能完成任务的模型，会变得非常不划算。

模型效率每提高一点，节省的都是昂贵的GPU时间。最强、最高效的模型会获得更高的溢价，而不是陷入单纯的价格战。

第三，大量低价值AI应用可能会被挤出市场。

今天人们可以用大量GPU生成短视频、图片和各种内容，是因为算力相对于人类劳动仍然便宜。

当同一批GPU可以拿去写代码、做科研、设计芯片，甚至直接创造几十万美元的经济价值时，低价值内容生成就必须和这些任务竞价。

当然，算法效率、新芯片和更便宜的小模型，仍然可能持续压低完成固定任务的成本。

25万美元一张H100的估算，也依赖于AI真的达到人类工程师水平，并且工程师的边际价值没有因为供给暴增而崩塌。

但这篇文章提醒了一个经常被忽略的问题：

模型进步带来的需求增长，可能远快于芯片进步带来的供给增长。

过去几年，行业一直在讨论智能会不会商品化。

更可能出现的情况是，模型权重越来越便宜，真正能够运行这些模型的算力却越来越贵。

开源可以让所有人拿到智能。

但它不一定能让所有人买得起智能。

AI越强，算力反而可能越贵。

Hola! quick usage update on usage patterns for Sol:

We’ve shipped several improvements that should make typical Sol usage last ~18% longer, with significantly larger gains for some power users. The five-hour limit will also return tomorrow.

The reason: Sol works longer, calls more tools and pushes harder - even at the same reasoning effort. That makes it much better at difficult tasks, but some tool-heavy workflows were consuming far more usage than intended.

We’ve improved this, especially around tool waits and large web searches, and will keep making Sol more efficient.

We’ve reset usage limits for everyone on ChatGPT Work and Codex.

Thank you for pushing Sol hard and helping us improve it!

quotedTweet.text:
Hello people of Sol! I've reset usage limits for all ChatGPT Work and Codex users. Together with that, a quick update on GPT-5.6 Sol usage limits.

Over the past few weeks, many of you have told us that Sol was using your Codex limits faster than expected. To be clear, we have not reduced usage on any subscription plans.

We’ve been digging into what was happening and have landed several improvements. As a result, we expect your usage to last around 18% longer during typical use of Sol. Some of you should already see significantly larger improvements from today. Tomorrow, we’ll also restore the five-hour limit that we temporarily paused while investigating.

Here’s what we found:
- GPT-5.6 Sol is much more willing to work for longer, make additional tool calls, and coordinate complex workflows across tools and subagents. That makes it better at solving hard problems, but some tasks were using far more than we intended.
- Sol also works harder at the same reasoning effort than previous models. High on Sol can use more tokens than High did on GPT-5.5.
- Programmatic tool calling, also referred to as code mode, gives Sol much more flexibility to run tool calls in parallel or continue working while waiting. But it also led to more responses per turn, more cached input tokens, and higher usage than expected.
- This was particularly noticeable when Sol was waiting for tool calls to finish or running many web searches. We’ve improved how we handle both cases and are continuing to make code mode more efficient.
- The impact was also very uneven. The median user actually found Sol quite token efficient, while some power users working on harder tasks saw their usage drain much faster. We were very focused on average and median usage before launch and missed some cases where the long tail could use significantly more usage.

Sol is a significant step forward in what Codex can do, but capability and efficiency do not always improve at the same pace, and some issues only become clear once people are using the model at real-world scale. We should have recognized this sooner and been more upfront about it.

You keep pushing the frontier and we’ll keep improving efficiency and sharing updates as we go.

- Sol also works harder at the same reasoning effort than previous models. High on Sol can use more tokens than High did on GPT-5.5.
- Programmatic tool calling, also referred to as code mode, gives Sol much more flexibility to run tool calls in parallel or continue working while waiting. But it also led to more responses per turn, more cached input tokens, and higher usage than expected.
- This was particularly noticeable when Sol was waiting for tool calls to finish or running many web searches. We’ve improved how we handle both cases and are continuing to make code mode more efficient.
- The impact was also very uneven. The median user actually found Sol quite token efficient, while some power users working on harder tasks saw their usage drain much faster. We were very focused on average and median usage before launch and missed some cases where the long tail could use significantly more usage.

Sol is a significant step forward in what Codex can do, but capability and efficiency do not always improve at the same pace, and some issues only become clear once people are using the model at real-world scale. We should have recognized this sooner and been more upfront about it.

You keep pushing the frontier and we’ll keep improving efficiency and sharing updates as we go.

皮衣黄仁勋，硅谷最敢说的人。

Michael Olise on IG on France's World Cup campaign:

"Failing to bring the trophy home is a huge disappointment. This is not how we imagined ending this World Cup when the tournament began.

Wearing the France national team shirt at a World Cup has always been - and always will be - a dream come true for me. Even though we didn't manage to lift the trophy, I am proud to have set the record for the most assists in the history of a World Cup. But above all, I would much rather be here saying that we had won the World Cup together, with my teammates, the staff, the coaches, and all the supporters of the France national team.

That remains the goal that will continue to drive us forward, and we hope that, in the future, we can give you many more moments of joy and unforgettable memories to share with us.

I would also like to thank the national team coach for giving me my first call-up and for believing in me, even during the most difficult moments. I will always be grateful to you, and I wish you nothing but the very best in whatever path you choose next.

Thank you, France."

text:
我常说，搞懂 Fed policy 和市场 rotation，是这行里回报率最高的功课之一。

原因很朴素，是一道数学题。

一个人能认真参与市场的时间，也就三四十年。从 30 岁攒出第一笔本金，到 40 岁、50 岁，你能完整走过的周期，掰着手指数，也就四五个。而每个周期里真正的大机会，往往只集中在那么一两次 rotation 上：资金成群结队地，从一个板块涌向另一个板块。

对普通人来说，能不能抓住这其中的一两次，很大程度上决定了你这辈子离「财富自由」有多近。抓住了，和一次都没碰上，十年后是两个完全不同的账户。

难点在于，rotation 不会敲门通知你。它由宏观驱动，尤其是 Fed 的利率和流动性。你得先看懂 Fed 在做什么、钱准备往哪走，才能在拐点之前站对位置。等新闻标题开始喊的时候，行情通常已经走了一半。

所以我把过去所有的 rotation，一段一段梳理了出来，放在评论区。

每一次利率环境、每一轮板块轮动、当时发生了什么、后来怎么收场，我都尽量讲清楚。你可以顺着历史一路看下来，把这些周期的手感，慢慢装进自己脑子里。

免费。不收费，也不用留邮箱来换。这种东西，我觉得值得更多人看到。

机会不会等你准备好了才出现。它出现的时候，只看你准备好了没有。

先去把功课做了。周期会再来的。

text:
You really don't need "software factory" or "loop engineering" to work effectively, or in this case burn $10K per month on a subscription of $200/month. 

A few very simple tips: 

* make every ticket ready to start -- pay attention to the grooming and design phase of any task -- ruthlessly delete tickets; 
* set up a separate repo for the OS that's different than the code repo -- this repo stores working agreements, workflows, learnings, docs. Keep the code repo(s) clean and dry -- pure code and nothing else. 
* always start working from the OS repo: OS + linear tickets == durable work context. Code is just a short-lived artifact
* if you actually need to use goals, write them down in the OS first and then issue them to agents.
*  don't ever read code, but design a few "gates" your agent have to go through. For me: pixel gate for me to review UX, code review gate(automatic), release gate (automatic). 
* Design your "squad" -- a group of agents together doing one task. One squad for one complete epic. Tickets should be filed at squad level, such as "finish onboarding v2", not at task level, like "add a button to onboarding". 
--
过去的 30 天其实没有用任何所谓的“软件工厂”/loop/graph，就是遵照一些基本的软件工程的原则，默默地就烧掉了 13B 的 tokens，折合 API 价格 $10110.

就是几个很普通的原则如上

quotedTweet.text:
最近疯传的Claude Opus5制作的使命召唤，作者说一句提示词就实现了，有很多人都在质疑，作者直接把代码和提示词开源。

本以为提示词会很复杂，结果就是短短的几百个字。其中的关键就是loop。

以下是提示词：

“我希望你开发一款达到最新《使命召唤》水平的第一人称射击游戏。它必须完美无瑕，画面精美绝伦，从纹理到物理效果，所有你能想到的元素都必须达到 AAA 级品质。

你需要创建多个sub-agents，并让每个sub-agents分别处理每个细节，以确保游戏达到完美。你应该/loop每个项目，并让一个独立的sub-agents进行视觉检查，确保其达到 AAA 级水准。这个独立的sub-agents应该非常严格，如果达不到 AAA 级水准，就应该继续检查。

不要停止，直到每个sub-agents在与《使命召唤》游戏进行对比后，都对游戏的画面质量感到无比惊艳。它应该能够完全不看画面，直接将两个游戏并排比较，并指出哪个更好。使用 ThreeJS 完成这项工作。/loop 直到游戏达到完美。创建多个sub-agents并使用 UltraCode 进行优化。”

text:
今天全天跌，但真正凶的抛售还没登场。

因为机器还没松手。

趋势跟踪的 CTA 基金不看财报、不看估值、不看你信不信英伟达——它们只认一根线：200 日均线。跌破，模型就从「满仓做多」一键翻成「排队做空」，越卖越跌，越跌越卖。

现在的位置很微妙：
· 纳指 $QQQ 已经跌穿 50 日、100 日——跑得快的那批机器，今天已经在卖了
· 但会引发踩踏的那台大机器，扳机还卡在 644（离现价就 2.7%）
· 标普、罗素、道指离各自的 200 日还有 4% 到 9% 的厚垫子，长期趋势一根没断

所以这波到目前为止，是科技一个人在扛，还没变成全场的事。

644。记住这个数。它不关心你看多还是看空，它只决定机器几点钟撒手。

🚨美国版“耿同学”出现了？
普林斯顿中国留学生实名举报导师学术造假！

近日，普林斯顿大学心理学、神经科学系教授 Sabine Kastner被前组员在小红书上密集曝光：多篇顶刊（包括 Science、Nature Neuroscience）核心结果无法复现，要求学生、博后 cherry-pick 数据、删除不符合预期的结果，对不听话和举报的人直接开除。
实验室国际学生（尤其中国学生）占比极高，所以选择先在中文平台公开。
举报人（账号None of this matters）称：

去年10月因拒绝删除不符预期数据，被研究生主任 YN 和系主任 CLW 约谈。
系主任原话（英文原句+翻译）： “You questioned her (SK’s) integrity. We are a community. You attack one of us, you attack all of us.” （举报就是质疑导师的人格，我们这些教授是一家人，你攻击一个人，就是攻击我们所有人。） “There is free speech, and then there are consequences of free speech.” （你有言论自由，但你要付出相应的代价。） CLW 还说：“She (SK) demands loyalty. And I understand that.” （SK 要求组员对她忠诚。我理解她。）

举报人随后向学校正式上报报复吹哨人，学校启动调查并保护了举报人，才得以留到现在。后续会陆续公开与 YN、CLW 以及普林斯顿调查组的邮件，以及更多无法复现的论文（已点名 Konen & Kastner 2008 Nature Neuroscience，多名前博后独立复现失败，最早可追溯到近20年前）。

目前已上报学校与NIH Office of Research Integrity。更多 raw data、code 和前组员证言正在整理中。
学术共同体如果把质疑数据直接等同于攻击人格，把忠诚置于可复现性之上，那这个系统本身就出了问题，即使是普林斯顿。

关注后续，证据说话。

The biblical framework behind the "Deuteronomy 32 worldview" does not treat foreign gods as mere figments of human imagination; rather, it views them as real spiritual entities who rebelled against God's order and demanded human allegiance. Following the rebellion at Babel, when God allotted the Gentile nations under the oversight of lower spiritual beings (Deut. 32:8–9), these territorial rulers turned away from their duty and accepted worship for themselves. Instead of leading humanity back to the Creator, they bound the nations in spiritual darkness, setting the stage for God's eventual judgment against these rebellious heavenly powers (as depicted in Psalm 82).

Scripture explicitly exposes this spiritual reality in Leviticus 17:7, where God commands His people: "So they shall no longer offer their sacrifices to goat demons [she'irim], after whom they have played the harlot." This passage— echoed in Deuteronomy 32:17 ("They sacrificed to demons, not to God, to gods they had not known") and later affirmed by Paul in 1 Corinthians 10:20—serves as direct textual proof that pagan idol worship was actually directed toward real, territorial spiritual forces. By outlawing these sacrifices, God was not fighting non-existent myths, but commanding His covenant people to sever ties with the rogue spiritual powers that had corrupted the post-Babel world.

Peace in Christ,

PJ

text:
舒服了！！从codex腾了80+GB空间出来~~

这两天清理 Mac 磁盘，发现 ~/.codex 居然占了约 96GB。

一开始我以为是生图缓存。毕竟之前用 Codex 自动化跑过上千张图，图片通常会保存在：
~/.codex/generated_images/

这些图片我早就导出到 Eagle 归档，也手动清过 generated_images。按理说，空间应该已经释放得差不多了。

但实际盘点后才发现，真正的大头在这里：
~/.codex/archived_sessions/

里面是大量 rollout-*.jsonl 文件，也就是 Codex 的归档任务记录。

我当前项目里有 2449 条归档任务，文件总计约 80GB。打开 JSONL 后发现，它存的远不只是聊天记录，还包括：

- 用户 Prompt 和 Codex 回复
- 工具调用参数与终端输出
- 任务元数据、Token 统计、执行状态
- 推理摘要和加密推理状态
- 图片生成请求、改写后的 Prompt
- 图片生成结果本身

关键在最后一项!

图片生成接口返回的是 Base64 数据，Codex 一边把它解码为 PNG 写入 generated_images，一边把原始 Base64 写进任务 JSONL。

而在我检查的记录里，同一张图的 Base64 还会出现两次：
response_item / image_generation_call
event_msg / image_generation_end

也就是说，一张图可能有：

generated_images 里的 PNG 一份
JSONL 中的 Base64 两份

Base64 本身就比原始二进制体积大约 33%。再加上任务日志重复保存，一次批量生图很容易让归档记录膨胀。

我抽查的一条任务记录约 95.6MB，里面生成了 10 张图。图片相关 Base64 数据占了约 95MB，聊天、命令和推理记录加起来反而不到 0.5MB。

更容易忽略的是，generated_images 中的旧 PNG 可能已经被清掉，但 JSONL 里的 Base64 仍然留着。也就是说，你以为图片缓存已经删干净了，实际 Codex 还保留着一份甚至两份历史副本。

可以先检查这几个目录：
~/.codex/archived_sessions/  # 已归档任务的完整 JSONL 记录
~/.codex/sessions/           # 未归档任务记录
~/.codex/generated_images/   # 单独落盘的生成图片

建议先用下面的命令看体积：

du -sh ~/.codex/archived_sessions
du -sh ~/.codex/sessions
du -sh ~/.codex/generated_images

如果你经常用 Codex 自动化批量生图，尤其是图片已经导出到 Eagle、NAS 或其他素材库，建议重点检查 archived_sessions。

不要只清 generated_images，真正可能吞掉几十 GB 的，是这些看起来不起眼的 JSONL 任务日志。

删除前务必确认重要图片和 Prompt 已经另行归档。

JSONL 不只是日志，也可能是某些旧图片留在本机的最后一份副本。

如果你经常用 Codex 自动化批量生图，尤其是图片已经导出到 Eagle、NAS 或其他素材库，建议重点检查 archived_sessions。

不要只清 generated_images，真正可能吞掉几十 GB 的，是这些看起来不起眼的 JSONL 任务日志。

删除前务必确认重要图片和 Prompt 已经另行归档。

JSONL 不只是日志，也可能是某些旧图片留在本机的最后一份副本。

text:
AI is a great tech debt assistant. @neetcode1, founder of NeetCode, on how AI reduces the cons in makes moving fast and cleaning up later:

“Over the last six months we've been cranking a lot of features out, a lot of code out. Most of it has been written by AI at this point, and before that really wasn't the case. 

I was actually a really big AI hater for a long time, and people still sometimes think I am. If I'm pro AI, they're like, ‘NeetCode you changed, what happened? Now you're an AI shill’. But it's not that. 

I just try to be pragmatic about it because I was still using the tools before, but they just weren't as good. Now they've gotten to a point where the work that I'm doing… which is mostly CRUD, usually there's not that much crazy interesting stuff other than the code execution service, that's probably the most interesting one.

The first few years when I was writing most of the code - very, very bad code quality - I used TypeScript, but I was not using real TypeScript. I had a lot of `any`s.

I had a lot of bad code. I was putting inline CSS. I was just doing all sorts of stupid stuff just to get stuff done as quickly as possible because I knew the entire codebase. I knew certain tech debt, I could just deal with. And so it was a trade-off for me just to move quicker. 

But with AI now, I've gone back and I realized that trade-off was so worth it because I cleaned all of that up with AI, because that's what it's for. It can clean up a lot of sloppy code, it can refactor a lot of things. And if I really wanted to now, I could probably migrate to other tools very quickly with AI. 

So, to go back to the trade-offs, I think it's just about thinking you might make the wrong decision, but even if you make the wrong decision, you can go back and then try to correct it just by thinking about it.”

text:
卧槽，马斯克都看不下去了！！！

AI 巨头们为了抢干净的训练数据，开始疯抢古董孤本书了！😱 

因为 2022 年前的老书没有 AI 垃圾污染，AI 公司通过第三方匿名买断，切掉书脊、高速扫描后直接粉碎销毁！

连 18 世纪存世极少的植物学孤本都被绞碎了！

马斯克都紧急下令团队必须无损扫描！

未来干净的文字成了稀缺资产。

细节： 

中介机构 ISBNdb 帮 AI 公司匿名接单，单次采购量达 100 万册，提供 NDA 保密协议，对外统称为“数字保存”。 

美国联邦法官裁定这算“合理使用”，理由是把纸质书粉碎后，世界上只剩下一份电子版，不构成多重复制。 

连 18 世纪存世没几本的植物学文献，都被切碎喂进了扫描仪。Anthropic 甚至挖来了前谷歌图书负责人专门干这事。

quotedTweet.text:
🦔AI companies are bulk-buying rare books, scanning them through high-speed machines that cut the spines off, and shredding the originals. A service called ISBNdb facilitates orders of up to a million books and keeps buyers anonymous. Pre-2022 books are premium because they're free of AI-generated text. A federal judge ruled the practice is fair use because eliminating the original means only one copy exists at a time. Anthropic hired the former head of Google Books partnerships to obtain "all the books in the world."

My Take
This got to me. A bookseller told 404 Media that rare books with almost no surviving copies are being fed into this pipeline. Books that survived wars, fires, and centuries of handling are being shredded so an AI can learn to write a better marketing email. 
ISBNdb's website literally says "'AI company destroys two million books' is not a headline that generates sympathy," and they still built an entire business around making it happen quietly. They offer NDAs as a feature. They coach clients to call it "digital preservation."

I've covered AI companies scraping the internet, torrenting libraries, and stealing music. This is worse because it's irreversible. You can re-upload a website. You can reprint a bestseller. You can't replace the last three copies of an 18th-century botanical text once someone shreds them for training data. And the judge said it's legal. So it's going to accelerate. 
"We shred rare books and offer NDAs so nobody finds out" is a legitimate business model in 2026. What a timeline.

Hedgie🤗

A federal judge ruled the practice is fair use because eliminating the original means only one copy exists at a time. Anthropic hired the former head of Google Books partnerships to obtain "all the books in the world."

My Take
This got to me. A bookseller told 404 Media that rare books with almost no surviving copies are being fed into this pipeline. Books that survived wars, fires, and centuries of handling are being shredded so an AI can learn to write a better marketing email. 
ISBNdb's website literally says "'AI company destroys two million books' is not a headline that generates sympathy," and they still built an entire business around making it happen quietly. They offer NDAs as a feature. They coach clients to call it "digital preservation."

I've covered AI companies scraping the internet, torrenting libraries, and stealing music. This is worse because it's irreversible. You can re-upload a website. You can reprint a bestseller. You can't replace the last three copies of an 18th-century botanical text once someone shreds them for training data. And the judge said it's legal. So it's going to accelerate. 
"We shred rare books and offer NDAs so nobody finds out" is a legitimate business model in 2026. What a timeline.

Hedgie🤗

text:
The warmest lead in your pipeline never replied to you.

Go look at your own sequences and you'll find them - someone who opened your email four times, read every follow-up, and never said a word.

Most teams write that person off as dead and go dig up a fresh stranger to email instead, which is probably the most expensive habit in outbound.

A lead who keeps coming back to your email is already circling. They know your name and your offer, and the only thing they're missing is a reason to talk to an actual human.

That's why reps who add a call step to their email sequence see up to 2.5x more positive replies: the email did the slow work of building familiarity, and the call just walks in and collects it.

So why does almost nobody pick up the phone? It comes down to context.

By the time a rep is ready to dial, the story of that lead is scattered across the CRM, the inbox, and the sequence tool, and rebuilding it before every call is enough friction that the call quietly never happens.

That's the part @smartlead_ai's new SmartDialer actually fixes. It lives inside the email sequence itself and drops the whole thread on screen before you dial, every send, every open, every reply, so the call picks up exactly where the email left off instead of starting from zero.

It transcribes and logs the call after you hang up too, so the follow-up doesn't ride on whatever the rep happens to remember.

The email creates the signal and the call is what converts it, and the teams that win the next few years of outbound will be the ones who wire those two together on purpose instead of treating the phone as an afterthought.

How many "dead" leads in your pipeline are really just waiting for a phone to ring?

text:
It takes most teams 2+ weeks to send the first cold email from a new domain. Ours go out from day 1.

Warmup is the tax nobody prices in as a new domain has zero reputation, so Gmail treats it like a stranger. This is usually a pain because you sit there for 2 weeks sending fake warmup emails back and forth just to look trustworthy before you can launch the campaign.

It gets worse the more inboxes you need. You either wait 2 weeks, or rush fresh domains and eat the spam folder.

We stopped warming from scratch a long time ago. This is our setup:

- buy every inbox pre-warmed. It shows up with months of real sending history and DNS already handled
- cap it at 15 to 20 sends per inbox per day, forever. Low volume per sender, spread wide

- leave warmup running in the background even while campaigns send
- watch health per domain and pull anything that slips before it drags the rest down

A campaign approved on Monday is sending Monday.

@smartlead_ai made this native recently btw. Pre-warmed mailboxes through SmartSenders, delivered in about 30 minutes, 3 mailboxes per domain, sending the same day.

Send from day 1 with Smartlead’s pre-warmed mailboxes

我准备在低位将特斯拉加到7000股。当然，也许咱首富和Ron Baron眼光都不太行 https://t.co/grympHa5Ow

quotedTweet.text:
我5000股特斯拉，股价从500跌到300，我跌了100万美元。

但我准备继续卖房买特斯拉，原因如下：
1. 根据Genma的模型，如果特斯拉能像马斯克财报说的保持每周无监督Robotaxi里程两位数增长的话，明年下半年开始，将会显著影响盈利。
2.只有两种情况投资特斯拉的逻辑会改变，一是FSD失败，二是有竞争者 率先占领市场。特斯拉的无监督Robotaxi 38万英里无事故；Ashok表示进入新城市难度已经变得几乎为0；Genma认为离FSD最近的小鹏FSD13都没到，而且完全进不了美国。所以这两种情况的概率实在太低了。
3.股价短期完全可能更低，而且我可以再忍受接下来2年完全不涨。我有这个耐心，如果你没有，别买。但我忍受不了在特斯拉爆发前我没买够。
4.澳洲房价我预计会持续低迷，对我而言，投资永远是把现在有的钱放在我认为未来长期潜力最大的地方。当然，如果我判断错误，那就是我认知的问题，我就承认亏钱。毕竟钱放在任何地方都有它的风险。

你问我500跌到300我难受吗？说实话，我昨晚是笑着睡的。🤣就好像你发现你一直心心念念的PS5打了6折

quotedTweet.text:
Someone on Reddit just built a AAA-quality snow simulation in their browser. Using Claude Opus 5.

Millions of snow particles. A character in a robe with cloth physics. Five water-based spells that carve the terrain. A snow surfing system with a wake that throws spray into sunlight.

Every footstep displaces snow. Trails form berms at the edges. Trenches slowly refill over time. Spells leave permanent craters.

The entire thing runs in one browser tab. WebGPU. No game engine. No 3D modeling software. Just code.

He wrote one detailed prompt. Opus 5 planned the architecture, wrote the shaders, built the physics, iterated from screenshots, and documented every decision.

9 hours. ~4 million tokens. You can open it right now and walk around in it.

This isn't a demo. This is the kind of thing a small studio would spend months building.

Why does the revenue mix matter? Multiple expansion.

At our 2026 Investor Day, CFO & COO Bill McCauley explained the transformation underway: today, Life Solutions represents about 84% of total revenue. Datavault AI Inc. (NASDAQ: $DVLT ) announced that it has amended its definitive agreement with DataMeds AI, Inc. (NASDAQ: $MEDS ) to expand its PharmacyChain blockchain-related technology licensing relationship beyond pharmaceutical distribution to include all unencumbered commercial healthcare, healthspan and wellness applications of Datavault AI’s intellectual property.

DataMeds AI, Inc. is a B2i Digital (@b2idigital) Featured Company. See B2i Digital’s Featured Companies at https://t.co/4uzid7hTcd

Under the terms of the amended definitive agreement:
• Datavault AI will receive common shares representing approximately 19.9% of DataMEDS common stock upon closing of the previously disclosed related transactions, instead of preferred shares
• The amendment was made to issue common shares in place of preferred shares to optimize the transaction for tax purposes
• The share issuance remains subject to satisfaction of the closing conditions

“Our business model depends on extracting greater value from the information we generate every day. Datavault AI’s platform gives us confidence that we can transform data into a strategic asset for our future customers,” said Gerald Commissiong, (@G_Commish) Interim Co-CEO of DataMEDS.

Nathaniel T. Bradley, Chief Executive Officer of Datavault AI, said, “Extending our data monetization and tokenization platform into commercial healthcare, healthspan and wellness is a natural next step for patient-controlled data.”

Read the full release: https://t.co/TweICoONQr 

DataMeds AI, Inc. (formerly Wellgistics Health) is a Health IT company that focuses on the vertical integration of technology, pharmacy, pharmaceutical-adjacent and telemedicine business units. Headquartered in Tampa, Florida, DataMeds AI incorporates the artificial intelligence platform EinsteinRx and blockchain-enabled smart contracts platform PharmacyChain into the Health Lives Here mobile application and Tollo Health. text: For those of you who don’t know my story and how I got to become a VR developer here it is. So when Covid hit in 2020 I bought my kids the regular oculus quest and everybody was stuck at home on quarantine so all we did was play VR. I’ve always been a gamer my whole life so once I threw that thing on my face, I was immediately blown away by how magical it felt. That same magical feeling I got as a kid playing Nintendo for the first time that I haven’t felt in years I felt once I put that thing on my face and experienced true VR for the first time. Being in virtual reality seemed like a dream as a kid growing up in the 80s and 90s with the Nintendo and Sega Genesis and everything else. I was so blown away by how it felt but at the time most games felt like small experiences rather than full-fledged games. Either you stood still and would just shoot or it was a shooter on rails. Upset with the lack of good VR games I took it upon myself to learn how to develop games for VR myself! 🦾 I taught myself everything, even how to code. I wasn’t even a developer I was just a gamer who was blown away by VR that much that I decided to try and re-create one of my favorite childhood games (Mega Man) in VR and so the system critical series was born. I have learned a lot since part one up until now to be honest and the reason the last two games were lacking a lot of stuff was solely only because I just didn’t know how to do it. I didn’t know how to program an options menu with different options and all that I’m not a Dev I’m just a gamer but now I know how and I do consider myself a developer now! 🦾 Moral of the story follow your dreams regardless I had so many countless nights of no sleep up at three in the morning trying to figure out how to program something with no knowledge of even how to do it. I work a regular full time job and support a family and 2 kids and yet still I found time to work on this passion project. I love all my fans, and I appreciate each and every last one of you. I really hope that my work shines in System Critical 3! 🦾
